points.speaker: Ted Cruz
points.quote:
Madam President, the Senate will soon pass landmark 
legislation to protect college sports. When any legislation, 
particularly landmark legislation, is enacted into law, there can be 
debate over that law's implementation. This isn't surprising. As the 
Senate prepares to potentially send the PCSA to the House of 
Representatives, I want to take a few moments to briefly explain the 
reasoning and intent behind some select, key provisions of the PCSA. I 
believe this will be useful not only for my colleagues here today, but 
for the PCSA's implementation.
points.summary: The Senate will soon pass landmark legislation to protect college sports.

points.speaker: Cory A. Booker
points.quote:
Well, this is a bill, going forward, where college athletes and the 
organizations that represent them have not had a seat at the table. It 
is a bill that was actually shaped by millions of dollars in lobbying 
from the NCAA and other powerful interests that control that industry. 
And at its core, it is a bill that undermines the rights of young 
people who pour their blood, sweat, tears, countless hours of work, and 
more into their craft. Their voices should have shaped this debate. We 
should have listened to their wisdom before voting today, before 
rushing to this vote as the last thing we do before a long recess.
points.summary: Well, this is a bill, going forward, where college athletes and the organizations that represent them have not had a seat at the table. It is a bill that was actually shaped by millions of dollars in lobbying from the NCAA and other powerful interests that control that industry. And at its core, it is a bill that undermines the rights of young people who pour their blood, sweat, tears, countless hours of work, and more into their craft. Their voices should have shaped this debate. We should have listened to their wisdom before voting today, before rushing to this vote as the last thing we do before a long recess.

selection.speaker: Ted Cruz
selection.quote:
Madam President, the Senate will soon pass landmark 
legislation to protect college sports. When any legislation, 
particularly landmark legislation, is enacted into law, there can be

selection.summary: The Senate will soon pass landmark legislation to protect college sports.
selection.reason: Supports the bill by endorsing the legislation as landmark and necessary.

selection.speaker: Eric Schmitt
selection.quote:
The Protect College Sports Act is built around a simple idea: 
athletes should be able to benefit from their talent, they should be 
protected from people who want to take advantage of them, and every 
school and every athlete should play by the same set of rules.
selection.summary: Athletes should be able to benefit from their talent, they should be protected from people who want to take advantage of them, and every school and every athlete should play by the same set of rules.
selection.reason: Directly states the bill's core proponent rationale for supporting athlete benefits, protections, and uniform rules.

selection.speaker: Eric Schmitt
selection.quote:
The problem is that college sports entered this new era without a 
stable framework to govern it. One court issues an order, one State 
passes a law, one conference adopts a rule, another court blocks it. 
Before athletes, coaches, and schools can adjust, the rules change all 
over again. This is the contradiction facing college athletics today.
selection.summary: The problem is that college sports entered this new era without a stable framework to govern it.
selection.reason: Supports the bill as a needed response to instability in college sports.

selection.speaker: Eric Schmitt
selection.quote:
The product is booming, but the model is breaking. Stadiums are 
packed, television audiences are strong, and billions of dollars are 
moving through the system; but behind the scenes, athletes and schools 
are trying to operate under a patchwork of State laws, court rulings, 
and conflicting standards. The Protect College Sports Act replaces that 
uncertainty with one national framework.
selection.summary: The product is booming, but the model is breaking.
selection.reason: Argues the bill is needed because the current system is unstable despite strong demand and money.

selection.speaker: Eric Schmitt
selection.quote:
An athlete in Missouri should have the same basic rights and 
protections as an athlete in California, Florida, or anywhere else in 
this country. A school should not gain an advantage simply because its 
State legislature passed a different NIL law. And a national 
competition should not be governed by 50 different rule books--that 
does not work in practice.
selection.summary: An athlete in Missouri should have the same basic rights and protections as an athlete in California, Florida, or anywhere else in this country.
selection.reason: Supports the bill on the ground that athletes should have uniform rights and protections nationwide.

selection.speaker: Eric Schmitt
selection.quote:
Just as important, athletes can keep making money. Let's be clear: 
this bill does not end NIL. It protects an athlete's right to earn 
money from his or her name, image, and likeness in Federal law for the 
first time. Athletes can still sign legitimate endorsement deals, work 
with local businesses and national brands, or hire an agent or an 
attorney. And schools can continue sharing substantial revenue directly 
with their student-athletes.
selection.summary: This bill does not end NIL. It protects an athlete's right to earn money from his or her name, image, and likeness in Federal law for the first time.
selection.reason: Supports the bill because it secures NIL rights and continued athlete compensation.

Their voices should have shaped this debate. We should have listened to their wisdom before voting today, before rushing to this vote as the last thing we do before a long recess.
selection.reason: This frames the bill as captured by powerful interests and as undermining athletes' rights, which directly supports a Nay vote.

selection.speaker: Cory A. Booker
selection.quote:
Mr. President, this is one of the hypocrisies in this 
bill. This bill targets athletes. It is subject to endorsement deals, 
redtape, scrutiny, and bureaucracy. It limits the amount of revenue 
that schools share with athletes, but there are no comparable 
restrictions on coaches or any other powerful actor in college sports. 
This strikes me as fundamentally unfair, especially when, during all 
these negotiations, college after college would whisper to me and say: 
There is a race to the bottom on these crazy coach salaries.
selection.summary: Mr. President, this is one of the hypocrisies in this bill. This bill targets athletes. It is subject to endorsement deals, redtape, scrutiny, and bureaucracy. It limits the amount of revenue that schools share with athletes, but there are no comparable restrictions on coaches or any other powerful actor in college sports. This strikes me as fundamentally unfair, especially when, during all these negotiations, college after college would whisper to me and say: There is a race to the bottom on these crazy coach salaries.
selection.reason: This states the bill is fundamentally unfair because it targets athletes while sparing coaches and other powerful actors.

selection.speaker: Cory A. Booker
selection.quote:
I know this bill is about to be passed, but I want to say 
very plainly, this bill sells out college athletes. This bill does not 
allow equal treatment between coaches and those athletes.
selection.summary: I know this bill is about to be passed, but I want to say very plainly, this bill sells out college athletes. This bill does not allow equal treatment between coaches and those athletes.
selection.reason: This directly argues the bill sells out college athletes and fails to treat coaches and athletes equally.

selection.speaker: Cory A. Booker
selection.quote:
This bill does not provide enough money left over for their health 
and interests. This bill gives permanent antitrust exemptions to this 
organization, and it does not create permanent protections for Olympic 
athletes, no permanent protections for women's sports, and this bill 
undermines the ability for athletes to sue for privacy violations and 
civil rights violations.
selection.summary: This bill does not provide enough money left over for their health and interests. This bill gives permanent antitrust exemptions to this organization, and it does not create permanent protections for Olympic athletes, no permanent protections for women's sports, and this bill undermines the ability for athletes to sue for privacy violations and civil rights violations.
selection.reason: This contends the bill leaves insufficient protection for athletes' health and rights and fails to protect Olympic athletes and women's sports.

selection.speaker: Cory A. Booker
selection.quote:
The Senate is on the verge--it really could happen tonight--of 
passing a bill that could reshape college sports for generations to 
come. It is a bill that was written without input from college athletes 
themselves, whose lives will be directly affected. It violates a simple 
rule: nothing about us without us.
selection.summary: The Senate is on the verge--it really could happen tonight--of passing a bill that could reshape college sports for generations to come. It is a bill that was written without input from college athletes themselves, whose lives will be directly affected. It violates a simple rule: nothing about us without us.
selection.reason: This argues the bill was written without input from the athletes it affects, which is a substantive reason to oppose it.

selection.speaker: Cory A. Booker
selection.quote:
Mr. President, I would like to speak about my amendment 
Booker and Blumenthal 6805. To my colleagues, college athletes are 
putting their bodies out there on the line every day. And many of us 
who played, we know that some suffer serious, long-term injuries to 
their spines, their knees, their shoulders, and now what we are seeing 
is the explosion of CTE, traumatic brain injury. It is a crisis in our 
country.
selection.summary: Mr. President, I would like to speak about my amendment Booker and Blumenthal 6805. To my colleagues, college athletes are putting their bodies out there on the line every day. And many of us who played, we know that some suffer serious, long-term injuries to their spines, their knees, their shoulders, and now what we are seeing is the explosion of CTE, traumatic brain injury. It is a crisis in our country.
selection.reason: This emphasizes the serious injuries athletes suffer and the need for stronger protection, supporting a vote against the bill as written.
